title: An HTML Canvas Graphics Device
text: cnvs small, heavily commented R graphics device, written learn R’s graphics devices actually work. renders plots JavaScript CanvasRenderingContext2D calls, embedded standalone HTML file – spirit archived canvas package webr::canvas(), intentionally simple C source (src/) can read end end someone unfamiliar R’s graphics engine internals. meant polished, general-purpose plotting backend: ’s raster image support, text metrics approximation (’s portable way get exact font metrics without actual rendering engine), one rectangular clip region tracked time. See comments src/device.c src/draw.c ’s implemented .

title: An HTML Canvas Graphics Device
text: result standalone HTML file: open browser, plot drawn live browser’s canvas engine JS commands R’s graphics engine produced. can inspect generated commands directly:
code: library(cnvs)  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html") cnvs(f, width = 480, height = 400) plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, col = "steelblue", pch = 19,      main = "mtcars: mpg vs weight") abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars), col = "firebrick", lwd = 2) invisible(dev.off()) cat(readLines(f)[8:18], sep = "\n") #> <canvas id="cnvs-page-1" width="480" height="400" style="border: 1px solid #ccc; margin-bottom: 1em;"></canvas> #> <script> #> (function() { #>   var canvas = document.getElementById("cnvs-page-1"); #>   var ctx = canvas.getContext("2d"); #>   ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 1.000)"; #>   ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 480, 400); #>   ctx.save(); #>   ctx.beginPath(); #>   ctx.rect(78.72, 78.72, 360.96, 223.36); #>   ctx.clip();

title: An HTML Canvas Graphics Device
text: custom graphics device implemented C, works registering table callback functions (one per drawing primitive) R’s graphics engine – ’s pure-R way intercept line(), rect(), text() friends. C source split responsibility: src/device.c – device lifecycle: building DevDesc struct, registering graphics engine, opening/closing pages. Start . src/draw.c – drawing callbacks: lines, rectangles, circles, polygons, text, clipping. src/colour.c – translating R’s packed colour integers, line styles, font descriptions equivalent CSS/JS. src/write.c – HTML/JS text templates everything else writes . src/cnvs.h ties together reasonable map whole device. R’s R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h headers (shipped every R installation) authoritative reference every field callback means.

text: package exists answer question "R graphics device actually work?" building one scratch R's public graphics device API (see R_ext/GraphicsDevice.h R_ext/GraphicsEngine.h R source tree, vignette("grDevices")-adjacent material). meant compete mature canvas-based devices archived canvas package webr::canvas() – deliberately keeps things simple (raster image support, approximate text metrics, single rectangular clip region time) source stays easy read end end. package's C source, src/, organised responsibility: device.c – device lifecycle: creating , closing , starting new pages. best starting point understanding device registers R. draw.c – drawing callbacks: lines, rectangles, circles, polygons, text, clipping. colour.c – translating R's packed colour integers, line styles, font descriptions CSS/JS. write.c – HTML/JS text templates everything else writes . text: Opens graphics device records subsequent plotting commands JavaScript CanvasRenderingContext2D calls, writing self-contained HTML file happen. new page plotting (instance, top-level graphics::plot() call, panel par(mfrow = ...) layout) starts fresh <canvas> element file, device left open across several plots produces several canvases stacked page. Close device grDevices::dev.() finish writing file.
